facts.fact: The Births and Deaths Registration Act (Cap. 51, in force 23 March 1973, amended 1994) has notice of a birth or death given on a signed prescribed form to the district Registrar, who signs it and forwards it by registered post to the Registrar-General, who alone keeps the registers of births and deaths; the Act provides for no electronic record.

systems.tiers: Notices are received by a Registrar of Births and Deaths in each district and forwarded to the Registrar-General, who keeps the registers

note: The held text is the Act's sections 1 to 22 and stops at the heading of the subsidiary Districts Order; the General Rules are not in it.
